items.text: Preferences controller's .then (controllers/preferences.js.es6:117-123) refreshes only name and bio_cooked, missing website_name

include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark (?) required by ActiveModelSerializers, so the predicate won't be invoked and website_name will serialize even when user fields are restricted (e.g., TL0/anonymous users viewing other profiles), leaking private data

Sibling-subdomain branch over-matches across shared or public suffixes - hosts with same label count (>2) and equal labels after first are treated as same site (e.g., evil.co.uk vs forum.co.uk, a.github.io vs forum.github.io)
Missing test coverage for sibling-subdomain branch, nil/blank website, unparseable URI rescue path, www-vs-apex case, and TL0/anonymous restriction on website_name

Sibling-subdomain branch treats hosts sharing labels after first as same site across public suffixes (attacker.co.uk vs forum.co.uk, a.github.io vs forum.github.io), showing full path for unrelated sites
No spec for nil or blank website, including that website_name is absent or nil - would have caught dead include_website_name filter

UserSerializer emits website_name whenever website is present, but does not honor Guardian#restrict_user_fields? like the website attribute does, causing TL0 users viewed by anonymous to leak website host/path via website_name
Host comparison is case-sensitive: http://Example.com/u does not match instance example.com due to missing downcase
include_website_name is missing its trailing '?' so active_model_serializers 0.8.3 never calls it, making the method dead and website_name always sent (as null when no website)
Same-domain URL with path '/' renders as 'example.com/' and port is dropped silently ('example.com:8080/u' shows as 'example.com/u')

Method `include_website_name` is missing the `?` suffix - the serializer uses `include_<attribute>?` as its predicate convention, so without the trailing `?` this method is never called and `website_name` will be included unconditionally

Regression: profile's website text becomes stale or missing after user edits website in preferences until full page reload - the removed client-side computed websiteName tracked model.website live, but new server-computed model.website_name is set once and nothing refreshes it

Same-domain matching is asymmetric - with website http://www.example.com/u on instance example.com, the else branch checks wrong direction ('example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com')), showing only host without path

The conditional serializer helper is named include_website_name (missing ?) instead of include_website_name? like all other helpers, which means it won't gate serialization as expected and may cause website_name to be emitted unconditionally.
Host comparison is case-sensitive - URI#host preserves case so http://Example.com/u does not match instance example.com
User#save (models/user.js.es6 ~166-215, 206-213) copies back only bio_excerpt from PUT response and ignores website_name, though users_controller#update returns full UserSerializer
website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, so TL0 user profile fields are exposed to anonymous visitors, undoing the anti-spam restriction on TL0 profile fields

Profile template may render a link/title using missing model.website (broken href) because the UI gates rendering on model.website_name but still uses model.website for the href/title, so when website is omitted the UI can display leaked text and/or create an empty/broken link

In website_name, the logic doesn't cover the case where the instance host is the apex domain (e.g. example.com) but the user website is a subdomain (e.g. www.example.com/user); in that case this branch returns only www.example.com without the path. Subdomains of the instance domain may need to include the path as well.
include_website_name is dead code - missing trailing '?' so active_model_serializers never calls it, causing website_name to always be serialized (as null when no website)

The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
website_name is over-built: parses URI(website) three times, calls discourse_host.split('.') four times, with nested ternaries that could be simplified to about 8 lines
No spec for sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) - the most complex branch with the over-match bug
Regression: website_name is now a static server value instead of a client computed property, causing the profile to show stale website name after user edits until full page reload

`include_website_name` method (line 153) is missing the trailing `?` - ActiveModel::Serializer requires the method to be named `include_website_name?` for conditional attribute inclusion, causing `website_name` to always be serialized instead of being conditionally omitted
The `include_website_name` method needs to apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` guard as `website`, otherwise the derived URL label can bypass the existing hidden-profile-field check
Asymmetric matching: website www.example.com on instance example.com shows host only, while reverse case shows path, missing the most common 'same domain' case

The `website_name` attribute is not included in `untrusted_attributes`, so it remains visible to anonymous users viewing TL0 profiles even though `website` is correctly hidden, leaking website information that should be restricted

issues.claim: The serializer method `include_website_name` lacks the trailing `?` that ActiveModel::Serializer requires for `include_<attr>?` predicates. As a result it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, as null when there is no website.

UserSerializer's `website_name` does not honor `Guardian#restrict_user_fields?` and is not in `untrusted_attributes`, unlike `website`. This exposes the website host/path of TL0 users to anonymous viewers.

The sibling-subdomain branch of `website_name` treats any hosts with the same label count (>2) and equal labels after the first as the same site, even across public suffixes. For example, `evil.co.uk` matches `forum.co.uk` and `a.github.io` matches `forum.github.io`, so the full path is shown for unrelated sites.
Tests are missing for the sibling-subdomain branch, nil/blank website, the unparseable-URI rescue path, the www-vs-apex case, and the TL0/anonymous restriction on `website_name`.
No spec covers a nil or blank website, including checking that `website_name` is absent or nil.
No spec covers the sibling-subdomain branch (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`).
The host comparison in `website_name` is case-sensitive because URI#host preserves case and nothing downcases it. So `http://Example.com/u` does not match instance `example.com`.
For a same-domain URL with path `/`, `website_name` renders `example.com/`. The port is also silently dropped, so `example.com:8080/u` shows as `example.com/u`.

Same-domain matching in `website_name` is asymmetric. With website `http://www.example.com/u` on instance `example.com`, the check runs in the wrong direction (`'example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com')`) and shows only the host without the path, while the reverse case shows the path.

The client-side computed websiteName that tracked `model.website` was replaced by a server-computed `model.website_name` that is set once. After a user edits their website in preferences, the profile shows a stale or missing website name until a full page reload.
The preferences controller's `.then` refreshes only `name` and `bio_cooked` after saving, not `website_name`.
`User#save` copies back only `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response and ignores `website_name`, even though `users_controller#update` returns the full UserSerializer.
The profile template gates rendering on `model.website_name` but uses `model.website` for the href/title. When `website` is omitted, it can render text with an empty or broken link.
`website_name` parses `URI(website)` three times and calls `discourse_host.split('.')` four times, using nested ternaries.
